items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: On tenor. Two tenors and we had a swinging time.

ctx.x: Organizing it. There was Vishnu Wood, Bill Wood on bass -- two basses, Eddie Blackwell and the three horns. I played -- just had one little concert, got my money, come on back to Brooklyn. The next job I had was down here at community college, Billy Higgins and I brought a group down. Played for the students through the help of Gloria and the Black Students League. Dee Dee Bridgewater was supposed to make it with us, but she had a prior engagement. So we brought Roland Alexander, Riane Kenny Zawadi and --

On tenor. Two tenors and we had a swinging time. Then -- what happened during that period? Oh, that's the time that my health really started failing. I wouldn't stop smoking cigarettes and I went to see the doctor. In fact, my lungs had been weak. He told me, 'I think you have emphysema.' That really didn't frighten me because I was fighting this alcohol and A.A. I'd make it a day or two and slip. I started having convulsions. Well, I was in kind of bad shape.
